ceiling_probe.result: FAILS the gate: deleting the entire pixel shader is worth 0.38 % of the pass, so no source-level change to it can matter. The workload is bound by the 100 draw calls of the city grid, not by shading

cost: 1 cycle: pristine copy, instrumentation, gated build, baseline, ceiling probe

anomaly.what: ablate_ps rep 1 came out 11.8 % slower than its own five other processes
anomaly.checked: every variant measured in 2T and 2U was tested for the same effect. No other r1 deviates by more than 0.3 % from its own r2+ median; the one other apparent case, 52_2t_w4/base at +1.04 %, is the cross-session drift already found and fixed by temporal pairing
anomaly.consequence: no earlier verdict is affected. The preregistered acceptance rule requires every paired process to be negative, so an outlier of this kind on a real candidate would produce a false rejection. The rule is not being changed after the fact; the protocol from here on is that a candidate showing one such outlier is re-run with more processes and both sets are reported
anomaly.cause: not established. It is not shader compilation - 200 warm-up frames precede the measured window and the region is a GPU timestamp median over 500 frames. A power or clock state on a GPU that had been idle is the likelier explanation, and it is recorded as unexplained rather than guessed
